Your Cafe Choices

  1. What do you usually drink at a cafe?

  2. Do you like cake or a cookie with your drink?

  3. Do you usually pay by card or with cash?

Typing practice

Type the text exactly. Timer starts with your first key.

Text to type: A cafe order can start with a drink and something sweet. At the cafe, Maya serves hot coffee and cold tea. Coffee can come with milk, while the cold tea can come without sugar. These details matter because two people can order tea but want different drinks. A small cup holds less than a large cup. Maya also serves cake by the slice and cookies as separate pieces. A slice of cake and a cookie are two different dessert choices. One person might want only a drink, while another wants both. The drink, its size, and the dessert are separate parts of the order. Clear details help Maya prepare the right things.

Typing practice

Type the text exactly. Timer starts with your first key.

Text to type: An order is easier to follow when its details stay together. The drink name tells the cafe worker what to prepare. Words such as small, hot, and cold make that choice clearer. At the cafe, Leo takes an order for a small hot coffee with milk. He repeats the drink details before preparing it. The customer listens and confirms that the order is right. A dessert can follow as another part of the same order. Leo then adds a cookie for this customer. An order can also include whether the customer will stay or take it away. This customer will stay, so Leo now has the complete order.

Typing practice

Type the text exactly. Timer starts with your first key.

Text to type: Payment comes after the order is clear. Here, Maya accepts both card and cash. A customer chooses how to pay before Maya finishes the sale. With cash, the customer gives money directly to Maya. With a card, the customer uses the card machine. The bill should match the food and drinks the customer ordered. In this example, Maya notices an extra cookie on the bill. She removes it before taking payment. The customer then pays by card and gets a receipt. Fixing the order first keeps the payment clear for both people.

Roleplay

Correct the Bill and Pay

Maya

Your bill is ready.

You

Sorry, I didn't order this cookie. Just the coffee, please.

Maya

I'm sorry. I've removed the cookie. The bill now has only your coffee.

You

Thank you. Can I pay by card?

Maya

Yes. We accept card and cash. Please use the card machine.

You

I've paid. Could I have a receipt, please?

Maya

Your payment is complete. Here is your receipt.

You

Thank you. Goodbye!

Speak

Make Your Own Order

  1. You are placing an order at a cafe. Choose a coffee or tea and a cake slice or cookie. Say your complete order aloud, including size, hot or cold, and milk or sugar. Then say whether you will stay or take it away and how you want to pay.

    Need a starting line?
    • The worker repeats the wrong size. Say a short correction aloud.

What you can do now

Final Reflection

  1. A clear cafe order includes the drink and the details you want. The bill should match your order before you pay. Which details matter most for your usual cafe order, and what would you say if the bill were wrong?

Reading

Drinks and Something Sweet

A cafe order can start with a drink and something sweet.

At the cafe, Maya serves hot coffee and cold tea.

Coffee can come with milk, while the cold tea can come without sugar.

These details matter because two people can order tea but want different drinks.

A small cup holds less than a large cup.

Maya also serves cake by the slice and cookies as separate pieces.

A slice of cake and a cookie are two different dessert choices.

One person might want only a drink, while another wants both.

The drink, its size, and the dessert are separate parts of the order.

Clear details help Maya prepare the right things.

Reading

Build a Clear Order

An order is easier to follow when its details stay together.

The drink name tells the cafe worker what to prepare.

Words such as small, hot, and cold make that choice clearer.

At the cafe, Leo takes an order for a small hot coffee with milk.

He repeats the drink details before preparing it.

The customer listens and confirms that the order is right.

A dessert can follow as another part of the same order.

Leo then adds a cookie for this customer.

An order can also include whether the customer will stay or take it away.

This customer will stay, so Leo now has the complete order.

Reading

Pay for the Right Order

Payment comes after the order is clear.

Here, Maya accepts both card and cash.

A customer chooses how to pay before Maya finishes the sale.

With cash, the customer gives money directly to Maya.

With a card, the customer uses the card machine.

The bill should match the food and drinks the customer ordered.

In this example, Maya notices an extra cookie on the bill.

She removes it before taking payment.

The customer then pays by card and gets a receipt.

Fixing the order first keeps the payment clear for both people.
